learning_outcomes.text: Students will grasp basic aspects of a specific future topic and become sensitized to the personal or societal challenges associated with it.

Students will be able to generate insights in inter- and transdisciplinary working groups and relate them to their respective disciplinary background. They will be encouraged to articulate and explain their own disciplinary perspective to others, as well as to adopt and discuss the perspectives of other disciplines.
Students will acquire transversal competences that they can apply in professional life and/or in the context of social engagement.

If students attend courses involving research-related projects, e.g., within the framework of research-based learning, they will generate research- and project-based knowledge. Depending on the application context, they will develop their own research questions, apply different research methods, and explain the results of their research.

Depending on the course format, students will communicate and cooperate in interdisciplinary working groups on the specific future topic. They will be able to reflect on and consider different perspectives and interests of other participants.
Students will be able to adequately assess their individual portfolio of future-oriented competences and use them profitably for their life and career planning.

assessment_rules: Graded examinations are not foreseen in the interdisciplinary Future Skills module. The selection of the ungraded examination type(s) is at the discretion of the respective lecturer, who adheres to the currently valid study regulations. A new examination form for the interdisciplinary Future Skills module (SkillsBook) is to be included in the ATPO as soon as possible. The module is passed when 150 work units have been completed, equating to 5 ECTS points.
